plugin.deviceenroll.intro: One QR code per group. Scan it on a factory-reset device and the device joins that group, takes the group's configuration, and is renamed to the next number in the group's sequence. Groups can share a configuration, so the applications you deploy stay in one place.
plugin.deviceenroll.rules.title: Enrollment rules
plugin.deviceenroll.rules.empty: No enrollment rules yet. Add one below.
plugin.deviceenroll.qr.nomainapp: No QR code: this configuration has no main application. Open Configurations, edit it, and set the Headwind launcher as the main app - the QR code has to tell a factory-reset device which app to install.
plugin.deviceenroll.form.hint: Each group gets one rule and one QR code. Point as many groups as you like at the same configuration - they share its applications and settings, and only the group and the numbering differ.
plugin.deviceenroll.configuration.hint: The configuration devices of this group are enrolled into. Sharing one configuration across groups is the normal case - it is what keeps application deployment in one place.
plugin.deviceenroll.configuration.nomain: This configuration has no main application, so it cannot produce an enrollment QR code. Set the Headwind launcher as its main app first, or choose a different configuration.
plugin.deviceenroll.saved: Enrollment rule saved. Scan the group's QR code to enrol devices into it.
plugin.deviceenroll.deleted: Enrollment rule removed. The group, its configuration and the devices already enrolled are unchanged.
plugin.deviceenroll.confirm.replace: This group already has an enrollment rule. Replace it? Devices already numbered keep their numbers, and the sequence carries on from where it is. A group can only have one rule, because the QR code identifies the group.
plugin.deviceenroll.confirm.delete: Stop numbering devices enrolled into ${name}? The group, its configuration and the devices already enrolled are left as they are - only the automatic numbering is removed.

plugin.devicelocation.intro: Where each device last reported from. Devices report a few times a day in normal use, and only the last few positions are kept. Report a device lost and it switches to reporting every couple of minutes, keeping every position until you mark it found.
plugin.devicelocation.coverage.missing.1: No position has ever been received from
plugin.devicelocation.coverage.missing.3: devices. Nothing is wrong with the map - those devices have not sent a position. The usual reasons:
plugin.devicelocation.map.hint: Click a marker or a device to see where it has been. Red markers are devices reported lost.
plugin.devicelocation.lost.title: Reported lost
plugin.devicelocation.devices.title: Devices
plugin.devicelocation.devices.none: No devices in this account yet.
plugin.devicelocation.trail.title: Where it has been:
plugin.devicelocation.trail.hint.2: positions per device. Positions recorded while a device was reported lost are kept in full.
plugin.devicelocation.trail.none: No positions recorded for this device.
plugin.devicelocation.confirm.lost: Report ${name} lost? The server will push it every couple of minutes to make it report its position, for as long as it is switched on and reachable, and those positions will be kept until you mark it found.
plugin.devicelocation.confirm.clear: Delete every recorded position for ${name}? This cannot be undone.
plugin.devicelocation.lost.reported: ${name} is now reported lost and will start reporting frequently. It may take a few minutes to pick up the change.
plugin.devicelocation.found.reported: ${name} is no longer reported lost and goes back to the normal schedule. Its trail has been kept - use Delete history to remove it.
plugin.devicelocation.error.map: The map library could not be loaded (${reason}). The positions below are still correct.
plugin.devicelocation.settings.intro: How often devices report their position, and how much of that is kept.
plugin.devicelocation.settings.keep.hint: Per device, in normal operation. Older positions are discarded as new ones arrive. Positions recorded while a device is reported lost are never trimmed.
plugin.devicelocation.settings.lost.hint: Once a device is reported lost, the server pushes it this often to make it report its position. 2 is a reasonable floor - shorter drains the battery without adding much.
plugin.devicelocation.settings.tileurl.h: The tile server the map draws from. The default is OpenStreetMap, which means the browser showing the map needs internet access. Point this at your own tile server to keep it inside your network.
plugin.devicelocation.settings.attributi: Shown in the corner of the map. Most tile providers require this.
plugin.devicelocation.settings.note.priv: These are positions of people's working devices. Keeping only a few positions per device is a deliberate default rather than a technical limit - raise it only if you have a reason you would be comfortable explaining to the people carrying them.
plugin.devicelocation.diag.tracking.2: device(s) has Location Tracking set to 'No active tracking', so the launcher never collects a position. Either set it to 'Track location by GPS' in Configurations > edit > Settings, or switch on 'Ask every device' in this plugin's settings and leave the configurations alone.
plugin.devicelocation.diag.forced.title: Tracking is being forced on.
plugin.devicelocation.diag.forced: This plugin is asking every device for GPS regardless of its configuration. A device picks that up on its next sync, so give it a minute - and check the launcher has the location permission.
plugin.devicelocation.diag.permission: A device reports its position with every sync, so a change here shows up on the device's next sync rather than immediately.
plugin.devicelocation.devices.hint: Every device is listed. Report one lost even if it has never sent a position - that is what turns close tracking on.
plugin.devicelocation.row.notracking: never reported - location tracking is off on configuration
Collect a position from every device, whatever its configuration says

Whether a launcher collects a position is normally a per-configuration setting that defaults to 'No active tracking'. With this on, the sync response asks every device for GPS, so a configuration created later cannot silently opt out. Turn it off to hand the decision back to each configuration.
plugin.devicelocation.diag.onhandset.tit: Nothing to collect on the handset.
plugin.devicelocation.diag.onhandset: device(s) have contacted the server in the last hour and still sent no position. That is a setting on the device, not on the server: the launcher needs the location permission granted and location switched on. On an emulator, also set a position in Extended controls > Location and press Set - the launcher reports the last known fix, and there is none until something provides one.
plugin.devicelocation.settings.note.norm: In normal use a device sends its position every time it syncs, and additionally every 15 minutes. That 15 minutes is fixed inside the launcher app and no server setting changes it.
plugin.devicelocation.settings.note.push: The lost interval works differently: the server sends the device a push asking it to sync, which makes it report. It therefore needs push notifications to be working. Without push, a lost device still reports - just on the launcher's own 15-minute schedule.
